headline: AI Features Need Product Edges to Survive Real-World Use
summary: Building successful AI products requires more than just a powerful model; robust surrounding software engineering is key to user experience and reliability.
details: Developing AI features effectively means focusing on the entire product, not just the model's capabilities. The article highlights that the surrounding software engineering—handling user interface states, network errors, and credit management—is crucial for a seamless user experience.

For instance, an iOS workout app using Claude via Supabase Edge Functions needs to manage AI feature availability based on user connectivity, existing generations, available credits, and context of existing data. This prevents frustrating user interactions and ensures the feature feels integrated.

Immediate UI state updates after a successful AI interaction are vital. This prevents the common issue where the backend registers a change (like a credit spent) but the UI remains outdated until a manual refresh, breaking user trust and flow.

Thorough testing of these surrounding components, including error mapping for connectivity versus backend failures, is essential. This ensures the AI feature behaves predictably and provides clear feedback to the user, avoiding vague 'unexpected server response' errors.

Ultimately, shipping AI features successfully is largely about applying standard software engineering principles to manage a probabilistic dependency. The surrounding 'contract' of the feature, ensuring it integrates smoothly with the rest of the application, matters more than the model call itself.

The true measure of an AI feature's success lies not just in its ability to respond, but in its resilience and usability within the realities of a production application. This means focusing on the user experience and reliability aspects that make it feel like a genuine part of the app.
